# SSH-001: Password authentication is off

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

With password authentication on, anyone on the internet can guess passwords against every account that has one, and bots do so all day. Keys cannot be guessed. A Match block that turns passwords back on for some users or addresses counts as a warning; Match all counts as global.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo sshd -T | grep -i '^passwordauthentication'; grep -ri passwordauthentication /etc/ssh/sshd_config /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/
```

## How to fix it

Add a drop-in with PasswordAuthentication no, named to sort before cloud-init's (for example /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-hardening.conf), then check with sudo sshd -t and reload ssh.

## What a fix can break

Accounts without an authorized key can no longer log in over SSH. Confirm a key login works in a second session before reloading.

Run `stackward explain SSH-001` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
